newsitem.title: USA: New Genome pact seen as big step.
newsitem.headline: New Genome pact seen as big step.

text.p: Genome Therapeutics Corp's partnership with Schering-Plough Corp to use genomics to find new therapeutics for treating ashthma is a major coup for Genome, pushing the company into the forefront of human genetics research, analysts said.

Schering-Plough's leadership in asthma treatments also lends credibility to Genome's technolgy and allows the biotech company to broaden its reach to human genetics from its previous focus on pathogens, or bacteria. Genome stock was up 11/16 from Friday's close to 11-1/4 in afternoon trade.
"This is extremely positive news for the company. It catapults it into a leadership position in the field of genomics," said Matt Geller of Oppenheimer & Co Inc.
On Monday, Schering-Plough announced a research collaboration, worth about $67 million to Genome, to use genomics for the development of treatment for asthma.
Genomics is the identification and study of genes associated with human disease for the development of diagnostics and therapeutics.

"This human gene alliance (pushes) Genome into the forefront of human gene discovery, as apposed to our past, which has been heavily focused in bacterial genetics," said Robert Hennessey, chairman and chief executive officer of the company in a telephone interview.

"This is a novel research effort...(directed at the) causal levels of asthma, focused clearly at the genetic foundations of asthma," Hennesey said. According to Hennessey, asthma afflicts 12 million Americans and its treatment represents a $2 billion market.
Hennesey said the company has already gotten a "substantial" front-end payment from Schering-Plough, declining to be quantify the payment.
He said that, when a specific compound was derived, Schering would pick up most of the work.
"Genome is more on the discovery end. Schering-Plough will take it it through the regulatory process," he said.
While Hennessey did not indicate the the time-frame for the collaboration, he noted that most alliances are designed to run for four to five years.

"Schering-Plough is a great company to have a partnership with. The (two companies) already had a partnership in pathogens and Schering was so pleased, that it chose Genome over other genomic companies," Oppenheimer's Geller said.

Genome's other collaborations include one with Schering-Plough concering Staph aureus, a major cause of severe antibiotic-resistant infections, and one with Swedish drug company, Astra Ab, for the development of treatments for H. pylori, a major cause of ulcers.
"This is our largest deal, the equivalent of both deals combined," said Genome's Hennessey, referring to the S. aureus and h. pylori collaborations.
"I think it was a tremendous announcement and that this is just the beginning. I think the future is very bright for this company," said Frederic Greenwald of Aegis Capital Corp.
"We view this deal as positive because it serves to both validate the company's science and broaden the focus of its technology," said Matthew Murray of Lehman Brothers.
Greenwald said that, based on the news, he thinks the price of the stock can reach higher than his previous estimate of $20 a share in the next six to 12 months.
Murray has a 12-month target price of $16 a share.
